Hadn't fully put it together but Hollywood financing is this wild mix:
• *VC-style bets* → fund lots of risky projects, hope a few become hits
• *PE-style contracts* → complex waterfalls, multi-party deals, backend points
• *Zero transparency* → even actors and investors don’t really know what they’ll make

A half recent thing that has been happening in Hollywood is that with the rise of the streaming platforms, residuals and other forms of compensation had to be rethought to accommodate the new landscape. Each streaming company and production company nowadays has a different form of compensation. Here is a very interesting semi-old article about the evolution of payment formats in Hollywood and a few of the discussions actors, production companies, lawyers and agents have been having with each other.

One thing that has been increasing again in the industry is the amount of big actors demanding production credits through equity ownership to try to avoid having to enter legal battles with the big companies for a fair salaries since the streaming viewership and the amount of runs of a specific show or movie on the streamings is virtually "immeasurable" by actors.
